title: Note-decay design: wire the recorded recall-outcome signal to the existing soft-retire primitive via an age-gated judge lane
summary: Finding behind the note-decay feature (task #1). (1) recall-outcome-journal is WRITE-ONLY today — appended at search time (routes/graph.js pending row) and at task-terminal (routes/overlay.js resolved row), but NO consumer reads the resolved win/loss-per-note outcomes back for any lifecycle decision; it feeds implicit-lift analytics only. (2) The SOFT-RETIRE primitive already exists: append note_superseded with validTo set and NO supersededBy (retire without replacement, per scripts/retire-continuity-notes.js) — a non-current note drops out of search_knowledge, the RAG candidate pool, and the judge orphan/edge/dup passes, while staying recoverable as bitemporal history (history / as_of). (3) Decay = the missing CONSUMER plus an age/opportunity-gated necessity slow-lane in lib/judge.js buildQueue that emits that soft-retire verdict; NOT eager-on-add, NOT a content-obviousness re-check (that bar is enforced at authoring time), and NOT a hard delete. Note importance is relational and empirical, not an intrinsic per-note scalar.
